BadRequest.description: Bad request, or a query parameter that is not allowed

Forbidden.description: Wrong Host (unknown_host), an Origin header (origin_refused), a scope the device lacks (forbidden_scope; see each operation's x-ainkrad-scope), or an operation marked x-ainkrad-destructive without a live step-up elevation (step_up_required)

Unauthorized.description: auth_failed (any signature or device failure, alike whatever the reason), clock_skew (with server_time), or session_expired

AccountDetail.description: What an `admin` write answers: the account and the runners its key may be leased to.

chain.description: The chain that holds the pool (set by `createAccount`).

pool.description: The pool the account joined (set by `createAccount`).

runners.description: Runner device ids, explicit (never a wildcard).

AccountHealth.description: An account's health counters, as the scheduler keeps them.

auth_streak.description:
A subscription's failed sessions in a row; the third keeps it out of new runs
(`state_reason` `auth_suspected`) until an admin answers.

fail_streak.description: Upstream errors counted in the current ten-minute window; three put it out for ten minutes.

last_success_at.description: The last time a request or a session on it went well.

plan_limit.description:
A subscription's latest plan-limit snapshot, as its harness last said it (harness output:
it can only cool the account, never disable it).

upstream_class.description: The last status class its gateway reported on any of its sessions.

AccountLogin.description: Where a sign-in has got to. Never a token or a code.

expires_at.description: Ten minutes after it began; a sign-in open past it fails.

reason.description: Why it `failed` or was `cancelled`; provider text passes the redactor.

state.description:
`starting`, `open_url` (open `url`, then send the code), `waiting_code` (the code is with
the runner), `storing`, `done` (see `account_id`), `failed` (see `reason`) or `cancelled`.

utilization.description: A fraction of the window's limit, past 1 at the limit.

AccountSpend.description: One account's usage. No key, secret name, delivery or runner: it is for a `read` device.

max_utilisation_bps.description: The highest used/cap of any limit, in basis points (10000 is at the cap).

recent_drops.description: Provider drops in the last hour.

AccountTested.description: What `POST /accounts/{id}/test` answers: a status class and a latency, never a response body.

result.description:
As [`LastTest::result`], or `inconclusive`: the provider's model list needs no key and its
definition declares no `test_path`, so nothing was sent and nothing is known of the key.

runner.description: The runner device that made the request (empty when `result` is `inconclusive`).

reply.description: Told to the agent; a denial's reason.

AgentSecret.description: A secret for the session: the broker's secret `name`, delivered under `var`.

var.description:
`[A-Z_][A-Z0-9_]*`, not `PATH`, `HOME` or a loader's: the value (`env` delivery), the
path of a 0600 file holding it (`file`), or of an askpass helper (`askpass`).

AgentSession.description: An agent session: a harness on a runner.

account.description: The account the session holds, whatever its delivery (an API key or a subscription).

agent.description: The opaque agent id the create named (the key of its chain binding).

attempt.description: Which attempt of its run it is, from 0.

chain.description: The chain as it was when the session began (an edit never moves a running run).

chain_id.description:
The chain the run draws its accounts from; absent for a session that names its account
itself or uses the runner's own login.

chain_pos.description: The entry of `chain` the run sits on, from 0.

failed_over_to.description: The attempt that replaced this one.

failover_class.description:
Why the run was moved off this attempt (`rate_limited`, `quota`, `auth`, `budget_pool`, …).
An ended run's last attempt says in `outcome.failover` (`{result, why, reasons}`) why it
could not move on. Admin only.

harness_session.description: The harness's own session id, what a resume continues.

repicked.description: How many accounts a launch refused after the pick before the one it holds (at most 2).

resumes.description: How many times it was resumed.

run.description:
The run it belongs to: its first attempt's id. A failover is a new session (an attempt) of
the same run; filter `listAgentSessions` with `run`.

secrets.description: The secrets it is leased at each start, by name.

skip_pools.description: The pools a budget stop took out of the run's chain. Admin only.

upstream_class.description:
The last status class its own gateway reported: `ok`, `rate_limited`, `quota`,
`server_error`, `auth_failed`, …

waiting.description:
Set while a chain session waits for an account: it stays `starting` until `until`, or
until `scheduler.wait_max_secs` ends the run.

body.description:
A harness event, or the session's own (`started`, `message`, `approval_request`,
`approval_decided`, `interrupted`, `gap`, `ended`), redacted.

seq.description: From 1, by one: replay from any `seq` with `after`.

AgentUsage.description: Tokens used, as the harness reported them.

cost_usd_micros.description: Millionths of a US dollar, when the harness says.

AgentWaiting.description: Why a chain session has not started: it waits for an account to come back.

since.description: Its first wait; it waits `scheduler.wait_max_secs` in all.

until.description: When the earliest account may be back.

why.description: A fixed phrase: every account the chain can use is cooling, limited or at its cap.

queued.description: `false` when this key was already used: nothing was queued.

AgentWakeRequest.description: A wake for an idle session.

key.description:
Makes the wake idempotent: asking again with the same key queues nothing (it is kept for
30 days). 1 to 128 of `A-Za-z0-9_.:-`; absent, the Core makes one up.

text.description: The next turn, 1 byte to 16 KiB; absent, the session just continues.

ApiVersion.description: The contract a server speaks: `/api/<major>` and its additions so far.

minor.description: Bumped on every additive change within the major.

sas.description: The SAS shown on both screens.

scopes.description: Narrower scopes than the pairing bound; never wider.

entity_id.description: A numeric entity id; absent for a device, which is named by `entity_ref` only.

entity_ref.description: The entity's public id: a device's opaque `d_…` id, else `entity_id` as text.

AuditPage.description:
A page of the audit log, newest first. `next_before` continues with older rows, absent on
the last page.

Chain.description:
An ordered fallback chain of 1 to 4 pools. A new session draws an account from the first
entry that has one to give.

is_default.description: The user's default chain serves an agent bound to none.

ChainBinding.description: An agent's binding: its sessions get this chain.

agent.description: The opaque agent id, 1 to 64 of `[A-Za-z0-9._:-]`.

ChainEntry.description:
One step of a chain: the pool tried at this position, and the harness and model its accounts
run. The harness is the pool's provider's own.

model.description: The model for that harness; absent, the harness's default.

challenge.description:
32 bytes, base64url (43 characters), opaque to the client; spend it once within
`expires_in` seconds.

options.description:
A passkey device's step-up only: `{"publicKey": PublicKeyCredentialRequestOptions}`
over `challenge`, for `navigator.credentials.get`.

device_id.description: The device that will answer it, `d_…`.

ClaimBody.description:
A claim. The credential hash is SHA-256 of the canonical typed code (upper-cased, dashes
and spaces dropped, `I`/`L` read as `1` and `O` as `0`: 10 ASCII Crockford characters), or
of the QR secret's 16 decoded bytes (not its base64 text). Vectors:
`crates/server/tests/vectors/pairing-v1.json`.

code.description: The typed code (`ABCDE-FGHJK`, any case); or `secret`.

pop.description:
The routine key's ES256 signature (raw r||s, base64url) over the UTF-8 string
`AINKRAD-PAIR-V1` LF `<core_fp>` LF `<base64url of the credential hash>` LF
`<fp(routine)>` LF `<fp(stepup) or ->`, no trailing newline; fp is base64url SHA-256 of
the SPKI.

pop_stepup.description: The step-up key over the same string, with `stepup_spki`.

routine_spki.description: The routine key: a P-256 SubjectPublicKeyInfo, base64url.

stepup_spki.description: The step-up key, where the device has one.

core_spki.description: The Core identity SPKI, base64url: its fingerprint must equal the QR's `c`.

device_id.description: The new device, `d_…`, pending until approved; for an invite it is active already.

pairing_id.description:
The pairing, `p_…`: with `core_spki` and its own key the device computes the SAS
itself and shows that, rather than trusting `sas` from whoever answered.

sas.description:
Show this; the approver compares it with theirs. The first 16 upper-case Crockford
characters of SHA-256(`AINKRAD-SAS-V1` ‖ core_spki ‖ routine_spki ‖ pairing id as
UTF-8), as `XXXX-XXXX-XXXX-XXXX`. Meaningless for an invite: nothing waits on a match.

created_by.description: `admin` devices: the device that made it.

expires_at.description: When the access token ends, when known.

grant_count.description: `admin` devices: how many grants say who may use it.

identity.description: The account or site the last test read (a GitHub login, an Atlassian account at a site).

is_default.description: The kind's default connection: used when several cover a call.

my_capabilities.description:
Other devices: what the caller may do with it (the capabilities of the grants that name
the caller); never anyone else's grants or limits.

ConnectionApp.description: Ainkrad's OAuth app for a kind, as configured: never a secret.

app_install_configured.description: GitHub: the GitHub App (repositories) is set up.

configured.description: Sign in works for the kind.

redirect_uri.description: Atlassian: the redirect address to register with Atlassian, exactly.

ConnectionAppField.description: One field of an app's config.

secret.description: A secret is write-only: only `set` is ever said.

value.description: The value of a field that is no secret.

ConnectionFlow.description: A sign-in as it stands: poll it.

authorize_url.description: Atlassian: what the Mac app opens in the browser.

error_code.description: When `failed`: a fixed code and a plain sentence with the fix.

identity.description: Once `connected`: who it is connected as.

sites.description: Atlassian, `choose_site`: the sites to pick from.

state.description: Atlassian: the `state` the redirect must carry; hand it back with the `code`.

user_code.description: GitHub: the code to type, large.

ConnectionFlowCallback.description: What the Mac app's loopback listener received. No `Debug`.

id.description: The Atlassian cloud id: what `chooseConnectionSite` takes.

ConnectionGrant.description: What someone may do with a connection.

limits.description: The resources it reaches, by the kind's limit key; none: any.

ConnectionKind.description: What a screen draws a kind's setup from.

configured.description: Whether Sign in works: Ainkrad's app for the kind is set up on this Core.

install_url.description: GitHub: where the person installs the GitHub App to choose repositories, when it is set up.

ConnectionUse.description: A use of a connection, from its audit rows: no payload.

code.description: The refusal code or the upstream class.

seq.description: The audit row's number: page with `before`.

CoreHealth.description:
What the Core can say about itself. A field it cannot know (no certificate on a loopback
Core, no backup yet) is absent.

cert_days_left.description: Whole days until then; negative once it has ended.

last_backup_at.description: When the newest backup (`<home>/backups/*.age`) was written.

uptime_secs.description: Seconds since this Core process started.

account_id.description: The Core account the attempt used, if it was one of Core's.

approximate.description: The turn was interrupted: the tokens are the meter's last reading.

cost_usd_micros.description: Millionths of a dollar; absent when the event is `unpriced` (never 0).

epoch.description: The attempt of the session (a restart or a failover starts a new epoch).

priced_at.description: When the list price that priced a `list_price` event was read.

connection.description: The connection used when several of the kind cover a call.

Device.description: A device: who it is and what it may do. Never a key's private half: the Core has none.

fingerprint.description: base64url SHA-256 of its routine public key: what pairing shows.

key_storage.description: Where its key lives, as the device claims it (not verified).

last_used_at.description: Marked at most once a minute.

scopes.description: What it may do (E1-09 enforces them).

stepup.description: Whether it enrolled a step-up key, so it can elevate (E1-09.3).

elevated_until.description: Until when this session may call routes marked `x-ainkrad-destructive`.

ErrorBody.description: A JSON error: a stable `code` and a message for people.

error_id.description:
`err_` and a ULID, unique to this answer: logged with it (and, for a refused write,
audited as `api.refused`), for the app's "Copy error".

server_time.description: The server's clock in unix seconds, on a `clock_skew` refusal only (handshake spec §5.3).

Event.description:
One entry of the event stream. `seq` only grows: it is the replay cursor, counted gap-free over
the events this device's scopes may see (`x-event-scopes`), so it differs between devices
with different scopes. New kinds may be added: a client skips an event whose kind it does not
know.

kind.description:
What happened: `audit` (an audited change; the payload is the audit row: `audit_seq`,
`action`, `actor_kind`, `actor_id`, `entity_kind`, `entity_id`, `entity_ref`, `details`;
a device is named by its `d_…` id in `entity_ref`, with `entity_id` null), or a kind a
module writes. The registered kinds are listed in `x-event-kinds`. The payload of
`agent.state` is `{session, state, reason, …}`: a chain session that waits for an account
says `reason: "waiting"` and `waiting: {until, why, since}` (`until` an RFC 3339 time, `since`
the first wait in unix seconds), and one whose launch refused its account, so another was
picked across a provider or harness, says `reason: "repicked"`, and a run a failover moved across
them says `reason: "failover"`, both with `from` and `to` (each `{provider, harness}`). `account.limited` is `{account, class, until, source}`: an account
cooled or limited until `until` (`class` `rate_limited`, `quota` or `plan_limit`; `source`
`gateway` or `harness`). `account.health` is `{account, user, state, reason}`: an account went
`unhealthy` (`reason` `upstream_errors` or `auth_suspected`). `account.failover` is `{run,
user, from_session, to_session, from_account, to_account, from_pool, to_pool, class, hop}`: a
run moved to `to_session`, or ended (`to_session` null: its chain has nothing left, the hop cap
or the storm guard; `to_account` is null while the successor waits for one). `account.budget` is
`{subject_kind, subject, state}` for an account's or a pool's budget (`state` `warning` or
`exhausted`). `account.expired` is `{account, user, reason}`: a key the provider refused was
confirmed and the account disabled. `alarm.raised` with `alarm` `failover_storm` and a
`user` says the bound on that user's failovers stopped a run of theirs from moving (once per
window and user). `connection.health` is `{connection, user, kind, state, reason}`: a connection's
health changed (`state` `active`, `cooling`, `limited`, `unhealthy` or `disabled`; `reason` a fixed
code: `rate_limited`, `quota`, `upstream_errors`, `auth_suspected`, `auth_failed`, `recovered`,
`auth_cleared`). It is visible to `admin` devices only (`x-event-scopes`), never to a `read` device;
the push for it goes to the owning user's admin devices only. No payload holds a key, a token or an
upstream's own words.

EventActor.description: Who acted, on an audited change.

Handshake.description: What the server is and speaks, for anyone.

api_minor.description: The contract minor this server speaks (`GET /api/v1/me` has it too).

git_sha.description: The commit it was built from (short sha), when the build knew it.

identity_fingerprint.description:
`core_fp`: base64url SHA-256 of the Core identity key's SPKI, 43 characters. Signed
into every request (handshake spec §5.2).

supported_minors.description:
Every minor a client may have been built against and still be served: 0 up to
`api_minor`.

HandshakeBody.description: A liveness proof request: a fresh nonce from the client.

nonce.description: 16 random bytes, base64url without padding (22 characters).

HandshakeProof.description:
`POST /handshake`'s answer: `GET`'s fields plus the proof, which is always present (review
L4). A client that pinned `core_fp` aborts with `core_identity_mismatch` when either is
missing or fails, and never falls back to `GET /handshake` (spec §13).

core_sig.description:
The Core identity key's ES256 signature (raw r||s, base64url) over the UTF-8 string
`AINKRAD-CORE-V1` LF `<host>` LF `<nonce>`, no trailing newline; `host` is the Core's
configured Host (the `Host` it requires), `nonce` the text the client sent.

core_spki.description:
The Core identity key, a P-256 SubjectPublicKeyInfo, base64url. Its fingerprint is
`identity_fingerprint`.

identity_fingerprint.description: `core_fp`, as in `GET /handshake`; a client checks `fp(core_spki)`, not this claim.

HostBinary.description: A program installed on the host, as the helper's manifest and checks say.

sha256_12.description: The first 12 hex characters of the file's SHA-256.

state.description: `ok`, `differs` (not the file the manifest lists) or `unsafe` (a link, or writable).

HostStatus.description: The Core machine as the host helper reports it.

bin_dir_safe.description: `/usr/local/bin` is root-owned and not group or other writable.

helper.description:
`present` (it answered), `absent` (no socket: not installed) or `error` (it did not answer
well: stopped, busy, too slow, refused).

host_id.description: The host's random id, set at install; an app pins it at first sight.

manifest.description: `ok`, `absent` or `invalid`: the state of the root-written manifest of installed programs.

since.description: When it entered its state, as systemd prints it.

runner.description: Absent when no local runner is installed.

expires_at.description: A runner invite's end (15 minutes); absent for a device invite, which never expires.

link.description: `ainkrad://connect?host=…&fp=<core_fp>&secret=…`, for a QR code: shown once.

pairing_id.description: `p_…`: reject it to withdraw the invite.

secret.description: The QR secret, base64url: shown once.

token.description:
A runner invite only, shown once: `<host>/<core_fp>.<secret>` (`host` as clients address
the Core), what `ainkrad-runner pair --invite` and `get.sh --runner --invite` take.

KindAuthMethod.description: One way to sign in to a kind, easiest first.

advanced.description: Shown under "Advanced", not as the first choice.

available.description:
`false` while the Core lacks what the method needs (Ainkrad's app is not set up yet, an
admin enters it with `setConnectionApp`): the screen says "not set up yet".

help.description: A plain sentence for the screen.

id.description: `oauth` (the kind's own sign-in), `app_install` (a GitHub App installation) or `token`.

steps.description: The steps the screen shows, in order.

KindCapability.description: A named permission of a kind.

class.description: `read` or `write`: a write capability is only ever granted by naming it.

KindLimit.description: A key of the resource limit a grant may carry.

LastTest.description: The last one-shot test of an account's key.

result.description:
The status class the provider answered: `ok`, `rate_limited`, `quota`, `auth_failed`,
`server_error`, `unreachable`, `refused_address`, `tls_failed`, `inconclusive` (see
[`AccountTested`]) or `failed` (the runner did not answer). Never provider text.

LatestEvent.description: The newest event's seq a client would be shown: the catch-up target.

floor.description:
The retention floor: events up to it were trimmed, so a client whose last read seq is
below it re-syncs (E1-04.4). Absent from servers before API minor 2.

LeaseGrant.description:
A granted lease: hand `lease` to the runner, which redeems it once before `expires_at`.
No `Debug` (review L4): a log line must never print a live lease.

lease.description: `l_…`; only its runner can redeem it.

LeasedSecret.description: A redeemed secret, for the runner only. No `Debug`.

expires_at.description: Drop it by then, or at the session's end.

LimitStanding.description: A limit and how much of it is used.

Lockout.description: A key that is locked now.

strikes.description: Locks in a row; each doubles the next.

LogLine.description: A page of a service's log, redacted by the helper, newest entries at the end.

next_before.description: Pass as `before` for the next older page; absent on the last.

LoginCode.description: The approval code the user pasted. No `Debug`: it is a one-time secret.

code.description: 8 to 512 of letters, digits and `-_.~#:+/=`; passed to the runner and dropped.

Me.description: The calling device and what the server speaks.

input_per_mtok_micro.description: List price per million input tokens, in millionths of a dollar.

Named.description: A device: who, by id and name.

NewAgentSession.description: A session to start. No `Debug`: the prompt is the caller's.

agent.description:
An opaque agent id (1 to 64 of `[A-Za-z0-9._:-]`): its bound chain, else the user's
default chain, serves the session. Needs `admin`. With no chain either way the session
runs as a plain one and names its harness.

chain.description:
A fallback chain's id: the session draws its account from it, one at a time. Needs
`admin`. It must not come with a harness, a model or an `acct.*` secret.

connection_access.description:
Capability names the session may call through its connections (`read_repo`,
`issues_write`, `read_issues`, ...; see `listConnectionKinds`). Needs `admin`. Absent: the
default, read-class capabilities only (write is an explicit grant); an agent's session
with none has no connection tools. An empty list is refused (400 `empty_allowlist`), and
so are operation names and `*` (400).

harness.description:
`claude`, `codex`, `opencode`, `agy` (what the runner's `agent` driver takes). Omit it
(and `model`) when the session draws from a chain: the account the allocator picks sets them.

model.description:
The model id as the provider names it. For a session served by the auth gateway it must be
one of the ids priced for its provider, exactly: the gateway resolves no alias.

secrets.description: At most 16. Each is leased to the runner at each start (secrets broker, gate G-SEC).

workspace.description:
The repo and worktree to work in (`{"repo_url", "base_branch", "branch", …}`); absent, a
scratch dir.

NewChain.description:
A chain to write: `[a-z][a-z0-9._-]{0,63}` and 1 to 4 entries, at most one of them a
subscription. For an edit this replaces the name and the whole list.

NewChainEntry.description: An entry to write: a pool and the model its accounts run.

model.description: A valid model id; an API-key pool's must be priced. Absent, the harness's default.

pool.description:
The pool's id; it must be the caller's user's, of a `claude`, `codex` or `agy` provider,
and in the chain once.

NewConnection.description:
A connection to make with a pasted credential (the Advanced way) or a GitHub App
installation. No `Debug`.

email.description: Jira token: the Atlassian account email.

installation_id.description: `app_install`: the GitHub App installation id the setup page returned.

label.description: What people see, 1 to 80 characters; absent, the kind's title.

token.description: The token or API token; written, never read back.

NewConnectionCredential.description: A replacement credential; the same fields as [`NewConnection`]'s. No `Debug`.

kind.description:
`device` (the default) or `runner`: a runner invite is single use, lasts 15 minutes, is
active at the claim with the `runner` scope, and needs no check code.

name.description: What to call the device that claims it.

scopes.description:
What it may do: within the creator's own scopes. A `runner` invite gets exactly `runner`
(this may be left out).

runner.description: The runner's device id, `d_…`; it must be in the secret's scope.
A runner device id; absent, the best ready runner that has the provider's harness.

kind.description: `device`, `runner`, or `passkey` (a browser, E1-08; only when the Core has passkeys).

name.description: What to call the new device.

scopes.description: What it may do: within the approver's own scopes; a runner gets exactly `runner`.

chain.description: An existing chain to put the pool in; default: the user's default chain (made if missing).

monthly_limit_usd_micros.description: The monthly dollar limit in micro-dollars; default 20000000 ($20); 0 is no limit.

pool.description: An existing pool of the provider to join; default: the provider's default pool (made if missing).

position.description: 0-based seat of the pool in the chain; default: last.

runners.description: Runner device ids it may be leased to; default none.

value.description: The API key; written, never read back.

runners.description: Runner device ids it may be leased to; default none.

value.description: UTF-8 text, at most `secrets.max_bytes`; written, never read back.

Page_Event.description: A page of a list. `next_after` is the cursor of the next page, absent on the last.

code.description: The typed code, `ABCDE-FGHJK`: shown once, good once, for 5 minutes.

qr.description: `ainkrad-pair:v1?h=…&p=…&c=<core_fp>&s=<secret>&e=…`, for a QR code: shown once.

PairingView.description: A pairing as the approver sees it.

key_storage.description: Where the claimant says its key lives: a claim, not verified.

sas.description:
The SAS the Core computed from its key and the claimant's: compare it with the new
device's screen, then send it back to approve.

code.description: The same code as for the options; or `secret`.

credential.description:
The created credential as a WebAuthn `RegisterPublicKeyCredential` (`id`, `rawId`,
`type`, `response.attestationObject`, `response.clientDataJSON`, optional
`response.transports`), binary fields base64url.

code.description: The typed code (`ABCDE-FGHJK`, any case); or `secret`.

expires_at.description: The pairing's expiry: the credential must be claimed before it.

options.description:
`{"publicKey": PublicKeyCredentialCreationOptions}` (WebAuthn, binary fields base64url):
ES256 only, attestation `none`, user verification required, a resident key preferred.
Decode it and pass it to `navigator.credentials.create`.

PastRetention.description: The 410 of a replay from below the retention floor (E1-04.4).

floor.description: The newest trimmed seq: every event above it is still there.

PolicyResult.description: The answer to a policy change.

policy.description: The policy now saved on the runner.

restarting.description:
The runner is restarting to apply it: it is offline for a few seconds and then reports the
new policy in `GET /runners` (`policy`). False when nothing it runs changed.

is_default.description: The provider's default pool serves an agent bound to none.

PriceBookEntry.description: A price: millionths of a dollar per million tokens, and when the provider's list price was read.

Provider.description: A provider definition: a built-in, or user data validated before it is stored.

key_prefix.description:
The shape this provider's keys start with (6 to 16 characters, never a built-in's, such
as `sk-or-v1-`). A definition that sets it holds keys, and then only through the gateway
(`delivery` is `["gateway"]`): the broker binds each key to the account's host by it.

models.description:

16 random bytes, base64url: offer `ainkrad.v1, ainkrad-ticket.<ticket>` as the
WebSocket subprotocols of `GET /api/v1/events/ws`. Good once.

device_signature.name: Ainkrad-Signature

info.description: The Ainkrad Core client API, for the Ainkrad app. Every request is signed by the device's own P-256 key (ES256, raw r||s): the headers Ainkrad-Device, Ainkrad-Session, Ainkrad-Alg (ES256), Ainkrad-Timestamp, Ainkrad-Nonce and Ainkrad-Signature cover an exact canonical string of the Core identity fingerprint, the method, path, query, time, nonce and the body's SHA-256 (handshake spec §5). A session comes from POST /handshake/challenge then POST /handshake/session and lasts 15 minutes; there is no bearer secret, and an Authorization header is refused. A signed body is at most 1 MiB: a larger one is answered 401 auth_failed and counted as a failure against the address, so keep uploads below it. Before trusting a Core, POST /handshake with a fresh nonce and check that core_sig verifies under core_spki and that its fingerprint is the pinned one. Requests carry the server's own Host and no Origin, or the Core's own origin from its web client. A web client signs in with a passkey (POST /handshake/passkey/options, then POST /handshake/passkey/session) and signs every request with a non-extractable WebCrypto P-256 session key in the same way; its event socket takes a one-time ticket (POST /api/v1/ws-ticket) in Sec-WebSocket-Protocol. Times are RFC 3339 UTC with milliseconds. Versioning: within /api/v1, enum values, union variants, optional fields and operations may be added; a client must keep an unknown enum value (every enum is open) and skip an event or union variant it cannot decode. Anything removed or renamed is a new /api/v2. `info.version` is `1.<minor>.0`; the minor (`GET /api/v1/me`, `versions.api.minor`) is bumped on every addition.

A step-up
Cancelled (audited as `account.login_cancelled`, event `account.login.failed` with the reason `cancelled`) and the runner told to drop it; one that already ended is returned as it is
Its state: never a token or a code. Only the device that started it sees it; 404 otherwise

The built-in providers, then the user definitions
Stored (audited as `provider.created`). 400 for a definition that fails validation (https DNS base URL, the harness's own variable); 409 `conflict` or `limit_reached`
Deleted (audited as `provider.deleted`); a built-in or one an account uses is refused

Deleted with its key, its leases and its pool seats (audited as `account.deleted`)

The concurrency cap, 0 (no cap) to 64 (audited as `account.cap_set`)

Cleared (audited as `account.limit_cleared`); `cleared` is false when there was no such limit; 404 for no such account

It raises what a session may spend, so it needs a step-up

With `chain` or `agent` (admin only, else 403): the session starts with no account and the allocator picks one from the chain (`waiting` while every account cools); 404 for no such chain, 400 for a harness, a model or an `acct.*` secret beside a chain. 409 `no_account` for a plain create of claude, codex or agy that names no `acct.*` secret and no credential variable of its own (it would answer "Not logged in"). A chain create passes a plain create's checks for the harness of every entry, and the runner must be online with room for at least one entry (else its refusal, 409 or 503), all before any row; an entry the runner cannot serve is skipped at the pick
One session
The waiting tool call is allowed or denied, from any device with `approve` (audited as `agent.decided`). 502 `runner_failed` when no such request waits
Its tool call in flight finishes, then it ends (killed after the runner's grace; audited as `agent.cancelled`)
Its harness is killed now and its delivered secrets removed (audited as `agent.killed`). A module's session: `admin` only, the break-glass stop when the module's own routes cannot
Given to the harness as its next turn (audited as `agent.messaged`, its length only). 409 `session_over`, 502 `runner_failed` when it is not running
